note.text: Adjectives typically modify nouns or serve as complements, as in a quiet room or the room is quiet. Adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives, other adverbs or clauses. Prepositions head phrases linking a complement, as in near the library. Conjunctions connect words, phrases or clauses. A word’s function depends on its sentence: fast can be adjectival or adverbial without an added ending.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify modifiers and connectors from their function in context. Builds on: nouns, pronouns and verbs. Leads to: paraphrase and sentence relationships.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original models: The careful reader checked the note carefully. The note lay beside the register. Bih stayed because a member needed help. Careful modifies reader; carefully modifies checked; beside heads a phrase with the register; because introduces a reason clause. Identifying functions helps explain why an edit changes meaning.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Underline the word being modified or the units being connected. Do not label every word ending in ly as an adverb without reading its use. Explain what relationship a connector expresses.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Careful and carefully have identical functions in every sentence. Correction: Forms must suit their role in the sentence.
Every modifier of a verb must be an adjective. Correction: An adverb can describe how an action is performed.
Beside is the finite verb in this phrase. Correction: The phrase expresses location rather than a finite action.
Because and although always express the same relationship. Correction: Reason and concession are different connections.

pick.q: In The folder is under the bench, what does under the bench do?
pick.r: Expresses a location relationship through a prepositional phrase
e: Is is the finite verb.
No reason clause follows under.
The phrase gives location, not quantity.
pick.y: Under heads a phrase with the bench as complement.

e: Although introduces concession, not the requested reason.
Unless introduces a condition.
Despite needs a different complement pattern here.
